content.text: Oh, I'm not a believer—not an atheist either. But I do respect her sacrifice.
Even if it was stupid and meaningless.
But, as I said before, there's no greater proof of loyalty than to follow a fool.
At least she died for a cause—her family legacy, her spirit of exploration, even that children's fairytale.
She was stupid, but she was faithful.

branch.text: Were you expecting a warning first? I thought you'd know better after what you've been through.
Sorry, but you won't hear any praise from me for a sentimental commander.
If I were your superior, I'd tell you to rip out your own heart and let the others see what sentiment leads to.
Oh, come on. You and I both know this isn't the end for her.
For someone as devoted as her, death is nothing more than the achievement of eternal life.
She's not like those blind followers who cut off their tongues. In fact, at this very moment, I fear she's being confronted with her own beliefs.
Join her now, while the gate is still open.
Or she'll leave you behind for good.

items.text: To a Skylark
Máhtu?
Are you there?

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: What-What are you suggesting, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: *panting weakly*

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: She's right. It's the only way to open the gate.
Máhtu, what are they talking about?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: We have no choice. Listen.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: You have to offer me to the gate.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What? No, Ms. Stranger! We—

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: You have to get through. You have to find Ms. Urd and stop the ritual. *cough*

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: My mission is to get you into the sanctuary by any means necessary.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, I won't allow it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No more sacrifices.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Have you heard of the lungfish?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It's an amphibious fish found in Africa. Its gills are so shrunken that it developed a second respiratory system—lungs.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It's an obligate air-breather, despite being a fish.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It's not a land-dwelling creature, but if it's kept from the air for too long, it'll drown in its own watery habitat.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A creature that doesn't belong to land or water ...

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Exactly. The Foundation is no home to me, and I just used the last of my moths to create that storm. I'm useless to them. If I go back there, I'd drown, just like the lungfish.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Let me open the gate. Spare me from drowning like the lungfish. Let me fulfill my role.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's a big world, Ms. Stranger. There will always be a place for you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We'll find another way to enter the sanctuary.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Radio, could you get Mr. Ulrich on the line? Perhaps he has another lead.
Máhtu, do you hear them? What are they planning?
What should we do? Should we join them?
Máhtu?
I don't ... What's wrong? Why are you so quiet?
Sing to me, speak to me like you used to, hum another verse of the Mother Spirit for me. Why don't you guide me?
It's because ... You were never there for me in the first place, were you?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen? How are you feeling?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Are you able to get up? Here, take these narwhal ivory candies. They might help calm your nerves.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Amundsen? Where are you going? Nautika?
Máhtu, do you know where Friele went?
Oh, she's gone to see the Mother Spirit, hasn't she?
But, that woman, she said that there is no "Mother Spirit."
Then, where is Friele now?
You forgot your pendant, Friele.
*sigh* How could you leave it behind? It's so important.
It's—

items.speaker: Friele
items.text: It's ambergris, Uncle Rolf!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Be careful, Friele! Gently! Look, there's something trapped inside.
A scalpel slides delicately over the ambergris, revealing a small stone that draws in the faces of an old man and a child.
Beneath the glow of the work light, the newly exposed milky pink stone shimmers with liquid radiance.

items.speaker: Grandfather
items.text: The reflection, the color ... What an interesting structure. This isn't like any rock sample we've studied before. How extraordinary.

items.speaker: Grandfather
items.text: It's not crystallized magma, nor any sediment I'm familiar with.

items.speaker: Grandfather
items.text: I believe this is a gift from Her, Nautika.

items.speaker: Grandfather
items.text: The great gift of the Mother Spirit.
The girl's fingers close around the pendant.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Grandpa said that it's a gift from the Mother Spirit, Friele.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I bet Antarctica is filled with all kinds of secrets about this little stone.

items.speaker: Expedition Team Members
items.text: "The harvest's bounty mankind's blessing be. We children, blind, from mazes must be free."

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'll find the stratum Grandpa never found.

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: Entering the ice zone. Grab your telescopes, explorers.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'll explore the eras Grandpa never explored.

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: The sextant was right. As long as we stick to this direction ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'll reveal the secrets Grandpa never revealed.

items.speaker: Team Member IV
items.text: Here. It's a Neptune bar—my favorite. It'll keep you warm a little longer.
I've never shown you this little piece of rock, have I, Máhtu?
Koht, Aase, Friele, and I ... We studied it over and over. We know it like we know the back of our hands.
When-When you came to me, I thought that maybe I would finally understand this rock and the Blank Era behind it.
You gave me hope. You gave me purpose. And you gave me the courage to face every obstacle.
You were there every step of the way, whispering in my ear, like a friend, like you were the voice of the Mother Spirit Herself guiding me to where I needed to be.
But now, now we must part ways.
This expedition has been like nothing I've ever done before. It's tested me and you to our limits.
So, I understand. You have every right to go your own way.
Okay, time for a proper goodbye.
Thank you, Máhtu, my little ear worm. Thank you for coming to me in this beautiful, terrifying place.
Goodbye now!
Even if you were never real ...
Just like the Mother Spirit.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Ms. Amundsen? Ms. Amundsen!

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: What do we do? She's not responding. It's like she's in some kind of trance.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I already gave her all of our candies. Maybe a calming spell will snap her out of it.
Plaza, City Ruins

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: *soft groan* What ... What's everybody doing here?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nautika! Thank goodness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You were caught in a trance. You weren't responding at all.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: What's happened?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The gate's closed. We're trying to figure out how to get past it without ... resorting to that.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Radio is currently trying to reach Mr. Ulrich so we can come up with a plan of action.
Nautika's vision sharpens as clarity returns to her.
Her sight finds focus on the closed gate as thoughts trickle back to her mind.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Lava tubes. Every volcano has them. They're pathways made by flowing lava that lead to the heart of the volcano.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: If we find one, we might be able to get to the sanctuary through it.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Not very likely.
No longer able to support herself, Ms. Stranger slumps against the face of the gate.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The entire volcano is under Manus Vindictae's control, and Animus has eyes on every possible route. Trust me. There's no way of getting in without her noticing.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Not even *cough* a squirrel could slip past her.
With a flick of her fan, she lets her vision rest on the gate once more.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's get moving up the mountain. We may still find a lava tube that they overlooked, or at least we'll have a better signal to get in contact with Mr. Ulrich.
Sonetto nods and steps forward, lifting the weakened woman to her feet.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Nautika, time to go.
Nautika gives a nod and fastens the pendant around her neck.
With a heavy thud, her backpack drops to the ground. After a short and purposeful rummaging, she produces a safety helmet and a pair of goggles.
A geological hammer and steel-pointed chisel now weigh in her grip too.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Alright. Let's do this.
She lifts her eyes and takes a step forward, then another, and another.
The others follow, heading out of the plaza.
Then she stops, casting one last look at her companions.
Nautika raises her hand. Her hammer shakes with pride.
Then, she kisses the pendant around her neck.
Just as abruptly, she turns back. Her snow boots grind into the snow, carving a deep footprint in the opposite direction.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Vertin, Sonetto, Ms. Radio! Goodbye!
She dashes away.
Straight toward the sanctuary gate.
Her sprinting strides grow faster and faster,
as she discovers a soaring power in her, one ready to erupt into action.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Ms. Amundsen! Where are you going?
Her friends swivel, moving to catch her.
Yet no one could hope to outrun this determined explorer.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'm sorry. I lied. The lava tubes don't always lead to the heart of the volcano.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But you'll find a way in. You will, because you must.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: And I, also, must find my own path, in my own way.
She's one step from the gate.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: NAUTIKA!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: My friends, my teammates.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I'm going away.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But you keep moving, okay? Don't wait for me.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: No! Nautika! Come back!
The pendant swings forward with her movement, cutting a decisive arc through the air.
She leaps up, fixing her eyes ahead.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: What's inside this ambergris, Grandpa?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: A new area for research? A message from the Mother Spirit? Or just an ordinary mix of minerals?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The mountains and plains beneath the snow and ice ... They're so very large and old. We're just so tiny and young compared to them, you know?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I think some secrets will always stay that way—secrets. No matter how much we explore.
Nautika lowers her eyes.
She smiles in the frozen light.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But still, if I get closer, look harder ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Maybe I'll see just a little bit more.
She lifts her eyes again.
A deep and utter silence pulses in the air before her.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Grandpa, I see it now.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It was the unknown that I was chasing, not answers.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It was the beautiful, glorious unknown.
One heartbeat.
The world stands renewed.
None among them even manages to catch the hem of her garment as it lifts in the wind.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Don't!
Silence returns, as if sound itself has drained away into a hidden funnel.
No wind. The lava lies still. The sun holds its place in the polar sky.
The gate.
Opens.
TO BE CONTINUED…
